article.title: JI announces Sept 3 nationwide strike over petroleum levy
article.summary: LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman has announced a nationwide strike on September 3 against the petroleum levy, warning that the party could march on Islamabad if the government fails to provide relief to the public.

article.title: Govt, JI agree to form committees to recommend reduction in petroleum levy
article.summary: The federal government and Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) on Thursday agreed to constitute committees to recommend measures for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to the public.JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah announced the decision at a press conference in Lahore.Addressing the press conference, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said a government delegation had met the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) leadership in Lahore.He said the government would constitute an expert committee and had asked the JI to form a similar committee to jointly discuss measures for reducing the petroleum levy.The governmentleviesRs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.“The government will happily act upon recommendations put forward by these committees,” Iqbal said, adding that both the government and JI agreed that relief should be provided to the public.“We requested them [JI] to form a team, and th...

article.title: Govt, JI agree to form committees to explore relief measures
article.summary: The government and Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) on Thursday agreed to form committees to deliberate on measures aimed at providing relief to the public amid rising inflation and petroleum prices.Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal, speaking at a joint press conference with JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, said the government had already constituted a committee and asked the JI to form its own team of experts.The development came as the JI continued its nationwide protest against the petroleum levy, inflation and high electricity prices. article.title: 6 JI workers arrested for allegedly burning motorcyles, tyres to obstruct traffic at Karachi's Korangi Crossing
article.summary: KARACHI: Six workers of the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) were arrested in Karachi on Wednesday on the accusation of setting motorcycles and tyres on fire at Korangi Crossing to block the roads, police said.The development coincided with JI’snationwide strikeagainst the petroleum levy, which the party said was being observed in a peaceful manner.In a statement, the party also seemed to distance itself from the burning of the two-wheelers and tyres, alleging that the government was resorting to “cheap tactics” to suppress its protest. Without naming anyone, the JI said “miscreants” were responsible for the Korangi Crossing incident.Videos — said to be of the incident — were circulating on social media and showed burned remnants of two motorcycles, alongside burning tyres laid out in a row to obstruct a road.
